newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast light crudes fall, lack of deals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast light crudes fall, lack of deals.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes fell with WTI/Cushing prices in a dormant Thursday session that saw most refineries balanced for March, trade sources said.
A small parcel of Line 63 crude sold for $1.00 over California Buena Vista crude, traders said. A L.A. refiner bought the 1,000 bpd contract for March.
Alaska North Slope (ANS) differentials stayed flat at $1.10 a barrel under March West Texas Intermediate, while BP, its leading seller, declined to offer a price.
Buyers, meanwhile, said they no longer needed to buy full cargoes of ANS for refineries production.
NYMEX March WTI fell as buyers sold off the contract before its expiration Thursday, traders said.
The decline in outright WTI prices pushed down ANS 70 cents a barrel to $20.75/20.95 a barrel.
Kern River crude was assessed $14 53/14.73 a barrel, with bids firming after most price discussion rose above last week's $3 discount deal.
